text:
sarah: Heads-up — we need to reconcile serialization expectations for the new staged pin metadata before we ship the rollout controller change.
mike: Which fields are we talking about? the current `pin` object is pretty minimal.
talia: We're adding `staged_until`, `compat_signature`, and `client_migration_version` as part of the staging flow.
jordan: Quick concern: older clients will ignore unknown fields, but we rely on clients to act differently based on `client_migration_version`.
olivia: Right — if older SDKs don't see `client_migration_version` they default to legacy routing which might bypass staged variants.
sarah: Proposal: servers include both old-style `pin.version` and a new `pin.meta` bag. Clients should prefer `pin.meta.client_migration_version` when present.
mike: That seems fine, but we must be explicit about the on-wire contract: server must keep old `pin.version` for compat; new fields are additive only.
kevin: Also we need to define semantics for `staged_until` — is it advisory (soft) or authoritative (hard)?
talia: My pick: soft by default. If `staged_until` is in the future, server may route to staged variant; clients can still opt-in/out via SDK flag.
jordan: For Private deployments we should allow an operator override so on-prem control planes can treat `staged_until` as hard.
olivia: Good point. Add `pin.meta.enforcement: "soft" | "hard" | "operator-override"`.
kevin: Telemetry wise: the server MUST emit `pin_resolution_source` metric: values {legacy, meta_soft, meta_hard, operator_override}.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout-controller@staged-pin-schema: deployed to staging (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:
sarah: Example on-wire snippet I sketched for the API response:

```
{
  "pin": {
    "version": "v2026-03-1",
    "meta": {
      "client_migration_version": "2",
      "compat_signature": "sha256:abc123...",
      "staged_until": "2026-04-15T00:00:00Z",
      "enforcement": "soft"
    }
  }
}
```

mike: Looks good. Clients should do: if `meta.client_migration_version > sdk.migration_level` -> show warning / opt-out flow.
talia: We should document fallback ordering explicitly: 1) operator_override 2) meta.hard 3) meta.soft 4) legacy.
jordan: And add a `pin.meta.hints` array for optional guidance (e.g., `prefer-lower-latency`, `preserve-response-format`). keeps extensible.
olivia: Migration plan: server returns both shapes for 4 weeks; SDKs ship a minor that reads `meta.*` but tolerates absence. Then after client adoption we can trim legacy field in major bump.
kevin: Who owns the rollout + observability checks?
sarah: I'll own the spec + docs. @mike will add server-side telemetry. @talia take SDK changes and compatibility tests.
mike: Ack.
talia: Ack, will open SDK PR and add canary tests.
jordan: I'll add operator-override support to the private control plane docs.
olivia: Let's add a liveness probe that verifies `pin_resolution_source` distribution doesn't fall back to `legacy` > 5% during canary.
sarah: Action items: spec PR by EOD, SDK PR w/ tests by next Tue, staging deploy already green. We'll reconvene after 1 week to decide on trimming legacy field.
mike: One more: ensure server preserves unknown `meta.*` fields when proxying between control plane and serving nodes.
kevin: Noted.
sarah: Thanks all. Keeping this thread as the single source for follow-ups. :memo:
